facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near her gluteal cleft
denied fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
a 4 × 4 cm area of swelling just left of the natal cleft at the level of the tip of the coccyx
mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin but no fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
no fluid was obtained
a complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass was excised from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx
the mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter
a high suspicion for abscess
the differential diagnosis at this time included inclusion cyst and soft-tissue tumor
percutaneous aspiration was performed in clinic
a 6-cm vertical incision was made over the lesion in the prone jack-knife position
the specimen was oriented with sutures and sent for permanent pathology

concepts.why: The patient presented with a swelling near the gluteal cleft, which is a common location for pilonidal cysts, and the presence of a complex and septated mass is consistent with this diagnosis.
The differential diagnosis included inclusion cyst, and the presence of a complex and septated mass is consistent with an epidermoid cyst.
The mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat, which is consistent with a lipoma, and the presence of a complex and septated mass is also possible in lipomas.
The differential diagnosis included inclusion cyst, and dermoid cysts can present as complex and septated masses, although they are less common in this location.
The differential diagnosis included soft-tissue tumor, and although less likely, soft tissue sarcomas can present as complex and septated masses in the subcutaneous tissue.

rationales.F01: The patient's history of progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft suggests a possible pilonidal cyst or other soft tissue mass.
rationales.F03: The location and size of the swelling are consistent with a pilonidal cyst or other soft tissue mass.
rationales.F06: The excision of a complex and septated mass from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx is highly suggestive of a pilonidal cyst or other soft tissue tumor.
rationales.F08: The initial suspicion for abscess is later ruled out by the lack of fluid obtained during percutaneous aspiration.
